results.title: Out Of Sync
results.overview: As everyday life becomes increasingly digital, older adults are expected to adapt to a world that was not necessarily designed with them in mind. ‘Out of Sync’ follows Maria and Grace as they navigate a digital world in their own ways, from figuring out unfamiliar apps and devices to making payments. Determined to maintain their independence, they encounter moments of frustration and uncertainty that reveal the hidden effort required just to keep up. Through their experiences, the documentary asks: as technology continues to shape our future, are we building a world that includes the generation that helped shape our present?

results.title: A Stone a Ripple
results.overview: Xiaodong once worked as a security guard at a university, where he nurtured a dream of making films, and for a time became known as the “inspirational security brother”. When the online fame faded, he returned to ordinary life. There he met Yuzhuo, who had left her family after illness reshaped her outlook. Their meeting was like a stone tossed into a lake, sending ripples across the surface.

results.title: My Funeral
results.overview: Have you ever wondered what the day of your funeral will be like?  Juanca is a ghost who visits his own funeral. He listens to conversations from the people he knows and discovers good things, bad things, and things he’d rather not know—even in death. From the afterlife, Juanca will try to do everything he can to clean up his legacy.

results.title: Little Guayule: The Lost Manzanar Rubber Project
results.original_title: Little Guayule: The Lost Manzanar Rubber Project
results.overview: Guayule, a plant native to the desert Southwest, is a natural source of non-latex rubber. During World War II, the Japanese Empire’s occupation of much of Southeast Asia meant that the Allies lost access to major sources of natural rubber.  In a remarkable story of skill, resilience, and ingenuity, Japanese Americans incarcerated at Manzanar and elsewhere worked to cultivate guayule and dramatically improve methods for extracting rubber from the plant. Little Guayule: The Lost Manzanar Rubber Project helps bring this little-known chapter of Manzanar history to light.

results.title: Like a Monster: a video poem in 5 parts
results.original_title: Like a Monster: a video poem in 5 parts
results.overview: Vintage filmstrips and projectors were widely used in classrooms during the 1960s and 1970s as educational tools. A filmstrip is a 35mm roll of still images that advances manually through a projector, often accompanied by recorded narration on cassette tape. Unlike digital video, filmstrips do not move continuously; the turning of a knob allows for pauses and reflection. Viewers are cued to advance the frames by a beep in the audio, creating a rhythm that emphasizes attention and shared experience. The project draws inspiration from Dada cut-up poems, in which clipped words from printed materials were rearranged to generate spontaneous and unexpected meanings.
